method: spec-vs-code audit of each RFC against main (d0a0314 + merged #28/#34/#35); every item carries file evidence from the audited tree

rfc-0001.title: Open institutional custody (core)

gaps.summary: Asset, ChainWallet, and Vault reach the signer inside SigningMaterials with no admin signature and no envelope hash commitment; only the destination is hash-bound (destination_hash). A compromised coordinator can supply a forged but internally consistent set and obtain a signature under another vault's rule. Not limited to zero-approval rules: preview_hash commits only to candidate id/revision, decoded-operation hash, and evidence hash, so a forged Asset.behavior passes exact-candidate approval unauthenticated, and bounded grants never use preview_hash (Codex review on the design doc). KeyDescriptor is described as signed in §7.3 but has no signature field.
gaps.fix_shape: Extend the envelope to commit hashes of asset, wallet, vault, and key descriptor the way destination_hash does. Protocol change: envelope schema and golden vectors; needs a deliberate compatibility decision, not a quick patch.
gaps.test_gap: A03 test mutates the wallet without rebuilding the envelope; add a consistently-forged-set test.
gaps.fixed_in: Option A implemented per docs/designs/signing-material-commitment.md under the user's decision 'A then B' (2026-10-26): the envelope (domain OIC/AUTHORIZATION/v2) commits asset_hash, wallet_hash, vault_hash, and key_descriptor_hash; the signer and the D2 replica execution boundary both verify them; golden vectors regenerated as a justified break. Hashes alone were not enough in D1, where the coordinator produces the envelope and the authority sees only its body hash, so a compromised coordinator could hash its own forged records; the signer therefore also pins the enrolled asset/wallet/vault hashes in TrustRoots.enrolled_materials (empty fails closed; key descriptor pinned by loaded-key equality). In D2 the replica additionally checks its pinned registry. Tests: forged-but-consistent materials, and a coordinator-built envelope over unenrolled records, are both refused. Merged in PR #39. Cost: enrolling a new asset/wallet/vault requires updating signer trust roots, like chain profiles. Option B: the pinned set is now an admin-quorum-signed MaterialEnrollment manifest (domain OIC/MATERIAL_ENROLLMENT/v1) that also pins the key descriptor; Signer::open refuses it without the quorum or for another institution. Its trust anchor is admin_keys, the same keys that sign destinations and policy; an attacker who can replace admin_keys can sign a new manifest.

gaps.summary: No destination supersession: an older admin-signed destination version stays signable forever. The kernel only checks the version equals what the proposer wrote in the intent; the only revocation is denying the whole destination id.
gaps.fix_shape: Enforce latest-enrolled-version at intent build/create (fail closed on superseded versions); longer term, an ordered destination registry in the authority.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the admin-signed MaterialEnrollment lists the destination_hash of each currently enrolled destination version, and the signer refuses an envelope whose destination is not listed, so a newer enrollment that leaves out an old version supersedes it at the signer, including for a compromised coordinator that bypasses the API. The signer persists the highest accepted enrollment epoch in its one-time-state ledger, so an older, validly signed enrollment cannot be replayed to re-enroll a revoked version. Test: superseded_destination_version_is_refused, older_material_enrollment_epoch_is_refused_after_a_newer_one.

gaps.summary: Most public API resources absent: no /v1/vaults, wallets enrollment, destination/policy/configuration proposals, freeze, or recovery-ceremony routes. Freeze exists only as a library call; no SDK directory; CLI has only demo and display-inputs.
EVM has no threshold backend (dev single-key signer; cggmp24 not integrated). FROST declares supports_refresh=false and supports_recover_or_replace=false.
gaps.note: Share refresh is a reserved design decision (RFC-0002 §3 decision 1); blocks A33.

gaps.summary: Admin changes have no delay, no before/after diff object, and widening vs narrowing a policy is treated the same. TrustRoots (verifier builds, chain profiles) are static per-signer settings, not ordered admin-quorum transactions.

No replacement or cancellation workflow after dispatch: candidate_revision hardcoded to 1, cancel returns IssuanceUncertain without invalidation, broadcaster refuses a second candidate, no gas-bump/same-nonce-cancel builder. Authority supports ReplacementPending.
One-time-state rollback fencing is local only: production callers open the ledger without an external high-water mark, so a whole-disk snapshot restore rolls back the sidecar too.

EVM verification thinner than spec: chain-id-only network identity (no genesis binding), fixed 65000 gas limit with no simulation, no L2 fee component, finality is a fixed confirmation count defaulting to 1 where the spec forbids fixed counts, no EIP-7702 delegation or allowance inventory.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the EVM adapter reports Finalized only for evidence taken at the profile's finality commitment (the chain's finalized view). Inclusion inside that view is final; the view already trails the head by the finality depth, so no second confirmation count applies. Before this, the live client's latest-head evidence with the default finality_depth of 1 made a transaction final one block after inclusion, and the broadcaster accepted that. Test observe_maps_lifecycle; chain-rpc live-node tests and oic demo pass. Remaining: chain-id-only network identity (no genesis binding), fixed 65,000 gas limit with no estimation or simulation, no L2 data-fee component, and no proxy implementation check.

gaps.summary: Solana delegate/close-authority checks run only on the destination token account; an existing source delegate is not detected; mint owner program taken from the registry, not evidence.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the source token account is now refused when it has a delegate or a close authority other than its owner (test spl_source_with_delegate_or_foreign_close_authority_is_rejected). Remaining: the mint account's owning program is still taken from the registry; verifying it needs a new evidence item from the chain clients. The transfer instruction targets the SPL Token program, which rejects a mint it does not own at execution.

gaps.summary: Evidence trust weakly enforced: trust_level is declared by untrusted callers, the bundle is unsigned, SingleProvider is blocked only when environment_id is literally 'mainnet', and pre-sign evidence is never cross-checked across sources.
API scopes limited to Read/Propose/Approve/Submit; spec also requires administrator, broadcaster, auditor, recovery roles. Webhooks are pull-only; WebhookSubscription type is unused.
PolicyRule has no vault-tier dimension; fees have only a per-operation maximum (no rolling native-fee budget applied).
gaps.fixed_in: Not fixed in PR #41, on purpose: a rolling native-fee budget changes ReserveRequest.exposure_limits, which the authority commits to and the D2 replica recomputes, so it is a protocol change with golden-vector impact. It needs its own PR with an optional, skipped-when-empty PolicyRule field so existing policy hashes stay stable.

gaps.summary: No TEE/HSM; shares sealed in software; development DKG runs on one machine. Gate D hardware scope.
No Bitcoin/Cosmos/Sui/Aptos/XRPL adapters; only NativeResource placeholder variants. Gate E scope; blocks A25-A29.

rfc-0001.covered: §3.2-§3.4, §5.1-§5.4, I1/I4/I5/I7 signer checks, §8 adapter contract, §10.1-10.2/10.4-10.5, §12.1-12.2, §13.2, §13.3 idempotency and error codes, §4.3 credential distinctness.

gaps.fixed_in: PR #36: the triage prose now matches the generated table; only A33 remains operationally blocked.

rfc-0003.title: Institution-operated signer network
known_fences_confirmed: A33 residual threshold power documented with a test
readmission is a development-only fleet-restart ceremony
roster propagation pending (SingleEpoch blocks committee activation)
BETA cfg gate in CI (lib only; node-runner binary uncovered, no N26 negative test)

gaps.summary: Attestation flow is a library with no network wiring: no VerificationRequest in peer-wire, nothing uses channel 11, no verifier node runtime, required_attestations policy absent, verifier-disagreement quarantine in memory only.

Networked lifecycle cannot pass ISSUANCE_COMMITTED: AuthorityRequest lacks RegisterIntent and Observe; intent registration requires a process on the authority host; SignatureObserved is local to the coordinator; D2 refuses RecordObservation.
D2 has no gateway submission path (Proposer::submit is replica-local; NodeApi 403s without a replica proposer) and no OpenFinalized/ReleaseFinalized coordinator driver.
D2 equivocation evidence (ConflictingNotarize/ConflictingFinalize/NullifyFinalize) is never kept or exported; ExportBundle covers D1 only; no N15 test.

Nothing publishes authority checkpoints to witnesses (consumer exists, no producer); node-runner opens the store without witness rollback detection; D1 reference topology has no witness node though §12 requires one.

All channels share one 128-entry inbound queue and one event queue; one flooding admitted peer starves Hello (5s convergence TTL) and authority.rpc replies, causing refused sessions and IssuanceUnknown.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: each channel has its own bounded inbound queue (drained round-robin) and its own bounded event queue whose sends wait their turn for the shared receiver. Real-socket test real_socket_flood_on_one_channel_does_not_drop_another_channels_message fails on the original shared-queue transport and passes on the per-channel one. Hello frames also get a dedicated inbound queue; that part is defense in depth with no test that fails without it (the receiver drains inbound queues continuously, so overflow at quota-limited rates was not reproduced). The test failure first attributed to Hello starvation was the sender's own flood exhausting its channel-0 quota, fixed by pacing the test flood.

gaps.summary: No metrics or logs from network crates; inbound and event drops silently discarded; handshake failures, roster divergence, session aborts, attestation disagreements, nullifications not exposed.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the node transport counts every dropped or refused arrival (inbound or event queue full, per channel; malformed, foreign-roster, and not-admitted frames), exposes the totals through Transport::stats(), and logs a tracing warning when a counter reaches a power of two. The flood test asserts the overflow is counted. Remaining: handshake failures, roster divergence, session aborts, and attestation disagreements are not yet counted, and no metrics endpoint exports the totals.

gaps.summary: Coordinator crash recovery: no reconciliation of in-flight operations on restart; approval expiry unreachable over authority.rpc, so a crash before Release strands reserved exposure.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: nothing in production called expire_approvals, so reserved exposure whose approvals expired stayed reserved. Authority::expire_due_approvals (commits only when a reservation is due, so an idle check is a read) now runs every 5 s on a background thread in the node-runner authority and the local stack, released when the authority is dropped. Test expire_due_approvals_commits_only_when_a_reservation_is_due. Remaining: the coordinator does not reconcile its in-flight OperationStore records on restart.

gaps.summary: Node API has 2 of ~11 spec'd endpoints (log, approvals); halt only via local IPC; no content-addressed gateway store; materials travel inline in SessionControl.
signer-core never measures its own build (checks only claimed hashes); Hello lacks the generation and build_hash fields.
Per-node journal incomplete: session rejection reasons, peer blocks, attestations not journaled; gateway/authority-rpc/transport keep no signed journal.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: signer-core journals every refused session open (Open and OpenFinalized) as signer.session_rejected with session, sender, and error code; status polling is not journaled, so it cannot fill the journal. Remaining: peer blocks and attestations are not journaled, and the gateway, authority-rpc, and transport nodes keep no signed journal.

gaps.summary: Class C data (intents, candidates, grants) plaintext at rest in journals and stores; disclosed in docs.
No networked DKG (CeremonyOpen/CeremonyResult absent); DKG is offline fixture provisioning; no point-to-point payload encryption to signer-core keys. Disclosed.
Halt key is a free-standing operator key, unbound to roster administrators; minimum_halt_sequence hardcoded 0 (no rollback floor); unhalt only in the local journal.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the signer keeps the highest halt sequence a node reached as a floor in its one-time-state ledger (Signer::ratchet_floor), raised after each halt command is durable and checked when signer-core opens, so deleting or restoring the halt file no longer un-halts a node even with minimum_halt_sequence 0 (test local_halt_is_signed_durable_and_stops_active_sessions). Remaining: the halt key is still a free-standing operator key not bound to the roster administrators; unhalt is journaled locally only; SignerFence and RosterActivate are not authority commands.

gaps.summary: Passkey sign_count parsed but never compared (no clone alert); no AAGUID allowlist.
gaps.fix_shape: Clone detection needs a persisted monotonic counter per enrolled credential. ApproverCredential is an admin-signed stored object, so adding last_sign_count is a schema and enrollment-flow change, not a patch.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the authority records each passkey credential's highest WebAuthn signature counter and refuses an approval whose counter did not increase when either value is nonzero (possible cloned authenticator); a replay of an already recorded grant still returns Conflict. Zero counters are not encoded, so existing authority state keeps its hash and golden vectors are unchanged. Test passkey_signature_counter_must_increase_across_approvals. Remaining: no AAGUID allowlist for device-bound authenticators.

rfc-0003.covered: §3.2-§3.3 roster validation, §4.1-§4.2 ACLs, §6.3 D2 re-execution, §8.1 Class S fences, §8.3 signed MPC frames, §10 generation fencing, §15 WebAuthn verification and proposer-exclusion, Stateright model.

rfc-0004.title: Operator console

gaps.summary: No authentication, RBAC, or scoping: boundary.ts gives CSRF-style protection only; one server-held bearer for every caller; Administration always visible.

Admin/governance screens are placeholder requirement tables; mutation button permanently disabled; no policy draft/simulation/diff, admin quorum, verifier handoff, offboarding, freeze/halt, recovery drill, credentials or webhooks.
No operations workflows (fee funding, sweeps, paused states) and no receive/deposit panel (no address or QR).
Case detail exists for sample fixtures only; real records get an inline alert; no case object, owner, RPC-disagreement/reorg handling, or identical-bytes rebroadcast.

Every non-OK mutation response, including definitive 4xx policy rejections, is flattened to a generic outcome-unknown message, dropping the backend reason; only a raw last_error code badge is shown; required_approvals parsed but never rendered.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #36 (route-scoped error mapping; backend detail never reflected) and PR #41 (the transfer detail states how many approvals the first matching policy rule requires, mirroring the kernel match_rule).

gaps.summary: Approval inbox filters on dispatch=ready without expiry/eligibility checks; no verifier deep link (CLI accepted per Q2); correctly no Approve button.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the approval queue lists a transfer only while it is before dispatch, not issued, and a matching policy rule requires approvals; the table shows unexpired grants against the requirement. The local count never hides a transfer, because the record keeps grants from credentials the authority may have removed. Expiry is judged at the time the state was read. The verifier stays the external oic-approve CLI, which RFC 004 Q2 accepts. Per-approver eligibility needs console authentication (0004-01).

gaps.summary: Raw state names; only FINALIZED_SUCCESS green, failures amber instead of red; no per-state labels/safe actions; no real-record operation timeline. Uncertain states correctly block retry/cancel.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: every lifecycle state maps to its RFC 004 §7 label and safe action, and §9 tone (green only for FINALIZED_SUCCESS; red for rejected, expired, failed, invalidated; amber for wait and uncertainty); the detail view shows the exact state. Remaining: a per-stage timeline with time and source for real records.

gaps.summary: Setup preflight hard-codes complete:true (spec forbids misleading success); release_signature_verified literal false; test-transfer step hard-coded awaiting; stale blocker still listed; no vault seeding or deposit step; checklist is a page, not persistent.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: the preflight step is complete only when the state database opened and took a write lock; the test-transfer step and the money-loop blocker reflect whether the console server holds the custody API origin and bearer. release_signature_verified stays false because nothing verifies it.

gaps.summary: Migration is CSV watch-only import only (works well); no manifest, semantic-gap report, canary, batch approval, or reconciliation.
No event search/filtering or sequence-gap detection in local mode; no global search; export limited to custody export plus first 1000 events.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: in local mode the transfers and approvals tables filter by a case-insensitive search across reference, intent, operation family, candidate, vault, wallet, destination (id, name, address), asset, and transaction id. Remaining: event search and filtering, sequence-gap detection, and a search box that spans every screen.

gaps.summary: Generic stale banner only; no per-scope age thresholds; balances shown without freshness check.
gaps.fixed_in: PR #41: each reconciliation checkpoint shows how long before the read it was taken, and reads as a current match only within CHECKPOINT_STALE_SECONDS (120); older matches are amber and labelled stale, exceptions red. A checkpoint without its timestamp is rejected. Remaining: available balances carry only a head height, no observation time, so they cannot get an age until the status API reports one.

rfc-0004.covered: Navigation matches §5; bridge/demo/watch-only boundaries (§3, §10) enforced: loopback-only upstream, route allowlist, idempotency key, body cap, demo write-block, watch-only never enrolls authority.
